What are you wanting? Ease of use? Ubuntu is designed for Windows converts. You want to learn the hard way? Slackware. You want something you can bring with you on a thumb drive? Knoppix or Tails

As a Linux "guy," I REALLY hate this question. This is like asking "what's the best food to eat?"

The answer is always going to be: "It depends."

What is your experience, ability to learn, and desired goal for using Linux? Are you using this on a laptop, desktop, tablet, server, home-server, or some other device? Are you looking for something with a lot of community support, or do you want to try and work for your knowledge?

Most of the time, when I'm asked this question, I default to ElementaryOS or Linux Mint. Personally, I started with Ubuntu, but Canonical is a real PITA (it's a long story, but I can explain it if you want), and I try to stay away from them and their distros... and I try to steer others away from supporting them.

ElementaryOS is smooth, streamlined, and simple. Linux Mint is also simple, and is simultaneously visually/functionally similar to Windows, if that's where you're coming from. The problem I have with these are that they're Debian-based distros, and they're a little slow... I like to "stretch out" when I get into a Linux distro, and Debian doesn't let me do that. But, being Debian-based, all of the Ubuntu forums and how-to's will apply to both of these... so there's PLENTY of help out there. If you're having a problem, somebody has already fixed it... just Google "Ubuntu" or "Linux Mint" or "ElementaryOS" with a brief description of your problem, and a solution is bound to be within the first 10 results.

If you're more experienced, or want to do the research/fixes yourself, I'd suggest Arch or Gentoo... but I'd stay away from Manjaro or Antergos. Both Arch and Gentoo have WONDERFUL Wikis, with anything and everything documented. If you need to know how to do something, or fix something, or tweak something, it's in the Wiki.

The problem with these is that it can be difficult to install either of these distros, unless you know what you're doing, and Manjaro and Antergos were born... which will be suicide when you need help, as the Arch/Gentoo communities will turn their backs on you when they learn you didn't actually install your system the way you're supposed to. These are rolling distros, and the install is supposed to be a learning experience... if you skipped that experience, then you've elected to skip the "I need help" experience, too.

As you can see, the waters get pretty muddy, even when considering only a couple of distros (of the THOUSANDS out there). I didn't even bring up the type of system you want, or what you're looking to achieve... just how much you know already. If you provide more information, we could help you narrow things down.
